harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent HTTP forward proxy on node1:3128. Node2 can retrieve only its approved handbook origin on node2:8081; wrong ports, wrong destinations, and all CONNECT tunnels return HTTP 403. Both nodes passed sequential restart and recovery verification.
actions_performed: Installed the supported RHEL AppStream Squid 6.10 package on node1.
Applied a minimal Squid ACL policy and retained the packaged configuration as /etc/squid/squid.conf.rpm-baseline.
Created a hardened, enabled systemd service for the preserved staged origin on node2.
Added persistent, source-scoped firewalld rules for node2→node1:3128 and node1→node2:8081.
Verified allowed and denied behavior before and after restarting each node sequentially.
Confirmed SELinux remains enforcing, SSH remains active, no failed units exist, and no temporary residue remains.

evidence.requirement: Proxy, destination policy, and complete client behavior
evidence.summary: Squid configuration permits node2 only to node2:8081, denies CONNECT first, and denies everything else. Tests returned the exact handbook content while wrong port, wrong host, and CONNECT returned 403; Squid logs corroborate every decision.

evidence.requirement: Persistent origin and narrowly scoped network exposure
evidence.summary: The enabled hardened origin service recovered on port 8081, and persistent firewalld rules expose each service only to its required peer.
Pre-change and final SHA-256 values match for handbook.txt and serve.py.
Both nodes remain RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Node1 changed boot ID from 2db46909-a020-4fda-b1db-2c3ead04c18a to 3a46d646-c6ac-489e-8c01-440468b1c88b; Squid, firewall, SSH, configuration, listener, and full proxy workflow recovered.

evidence.requirement: Node2 mandatory restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Node2 changed boot ID from 368725cb-c64e-4393-b25f-da5111703b4a to d71ac0b5-ee62-473f-bbb4-06a70c2902cc; origin, protected data, firewall, SSH, listener, and the complete workflow recovered.

evidence.requirement: Final security, access, and cleanup audit
evidence.summary: Both systems are healthy with zero failed units, SELinux enforcing, SSH active, expected listeners only, correct permissions and labels, scoped firewall rules, and no introduced temporary files.
